chapters.name: Cardiology
chapters.blurb: Ischemic disease, valvular lesions, rhythm disturbance, and vascular emergencies.

topics.title: Stable angina
topics.summary: Exertional chest pressure relieved by rest with reproducible substernal discomfort brought on by climbing stairs is the presentation that defines stable angina. Exercise stress testing confirms it, and antianginal therapy with a beta blocker is the initial management.

topics.title: Acute pericarditis
topics.summary: Sharp pleuritic chest pain that improves with sitting forward with a scratchy triphasic friction rub at the left sternal border is the presentation that defines acute pericarditis. Electrocardiography confirms it, and a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug plus colchicine is the initial management.

topics.title: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
topics.topic: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
topics.summary: Progressive exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, and ankle swelling with bibasilar crackles, jugular venous distension, and an S3 gallop is the presentation that defines heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Transthoracic echocardiography confirms it, and guideline-directed medical therapy beginning with a renin-angiotensin antagonist and a beta blocker is the initial management.

topics.title: Atrial fibrillation
topics.summary: Intermittent palpitations with lightheadedness with an irregularly irregular pulse without discrete P waves on the monitor is the presentation that defines atrial fibrillation. Electrocardiography confirms it, and rate control and anticoagulation guided by a validated risk score is the initial management.

topics.title: Aortic stenosis
topics.summary: Exertional dyspnea and a single episode of near-syncope with a late-peaking crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur radiating to the carotids is the presentation that defines aortic stenosis. Transthoracic echocardiography confirms it, and referral for valve replacement evaluation is the initial management.

topics.title: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
topics.summary: Exertional syncope during competitive sport with a harsh systolic murmur that grows louder with the Valsalva maneuver is the presentation that defines hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Transthoracic echocardiography confirms it, and a beta blocker with counseling on activity and family screening is the initial management.

topics.title: Infective endocarditis
topics.summary: Two weeks of fever, night sweats, and malaise with splinter hemorrhages and a new holosystolic murmur at the apex is the presentation that defines infective endocarditis. Serial blood cultures followed by echocardiography confirms it, and empiric intravenous antibiotic therapy after cultures are drawn is the initial management.

topics.title: Aortic dissection
topics.summary: Abrupt tearing chest pain radiating to the interscapular region with a 24 mm Hg blood pressure difference between the arms is the presentation that defines aortic dissection. CT angiography of the chest confirms it, and immediate intravenous control of heart rate and blood pressure is the initial management.

topics.title: Deep venous thrombosis
topics.summary: Three days of unilateral calf swelling and aching with asymmetric pitting edema with tenderness along the deep venous system is the presentation that defines deep venous thrombosis. Compression ultrasonography of the leg confirms it, and therapeutic anticoagulation is the initial management.

topics.title: Peripheral artery disease
topics.summary: Calf pain after two blocks of walking, relieved by standing still with diminished pedal pulses with shiny, hairless skin over the shins is the presentation that defines peripheral artery disease. Ankle-brachial index measurement confirms it, and a supervised exercise program with aggressive risk factor modification is the initial management.

topics.title: Acute coronary syndrome
topics.summary: Thirty minutes of crushing substernal chest pain at rest with diaphoresis with dynamic ST-segment depression on serial tracings is the presentation that defines acute coronary syndrome. Serial troponin measurement with continuous electrocardiography confirms it, and dual antiplatelet therapy and urgent reperfusion evaluation is the initial management.

topics.title: Mitral regurgitation
topics.summary: Slowly progressive dyspnea with fatigue on exertion with a holosystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla is the presentation that defines mitral regurgitation. Transthoracic echocardiography confirms it, and serial imaging with surgical referral once severity criteria are met is the initial management.

chapters.name: Pulmonology
chapters.blurb: Airway disease, parenchymal and pleural disorders, and respiratory failure.

topics.title: Community-acquired pneumonia
topics.summary: Three days of productive cough, fever, and pleuritic chest pain with focal crackles with egophony over the right lower lung field is the presentation that defines community-acquired pneumonia. Chest radiography confirms it, and empiric antibiotic therapy guided by a severity score is the initial management.

topics.title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation
topics.summary: Two days of worsening dyspnea with increased sputum purulence with diffuse expiratory wheezing with a prolonged expiratory phase is the presentation that defines chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation. Arterial blood gas analysis with chest radiography confirms it, and inhaled bronchodilators, systemic glucocorticoids, and antibiotics when criteria are met is the initial management.

topics.title: Pulmonary embolism
topics.summary: Sudden pleuritic chest pain with unexplained breathlessness with tachycardia and an oxygen saturation of 89% on room air is the presentation that defines pulmonary embolism. CT pulmonary angiography selected by pre-test probability confirms it, and therapeutic anticoagulation is the initial management.

topics.title: Asthma
topics.summary: Episodic wheezing and nocturnal cough triggered by cold air with diffuse polyphonic wheezes that clear after bronchodilator administration is the presentation that defines asthma. Spirometry with bronchodilator responsiveness testing confirms it, and an inhaled corticosteroid-containing controller regimen is the initial management.

topics.title: Obstructive sleep apnea
topics.summary: Loud snoring with witnessed pauses and daytime sleepiness with a crowded oropharynx with an elevated neck circumference is the presentation that defines obstructive sleep apnea. Overnight polysomnography or home sleep apnea testing confirms it, and positive airway pressure therapy with weight management is the initial management.

topics.title: Pleural effusion
topics.summary: Gradually progressive dyspnea and a dry cough with dullness to percussion with absent breath sounds at the left base is the presentation that defines pleural effusion. Thoracentesis with pleural fluid analysis confirms it, and drainage and treatment directed at the underlying cause is the initial management.

topics.title: Pneumothorax
topics.summary: Abrupt unilateral chest pain with breathlessness at rest with absent breath sounds and hyperresonance over one hemithorax is the presentation that defines pneumothorax. Upright chest radiography confirms it, and observation with oxygen for small collections; catheter drainage when large is the initial management.

topics.title: Interstitial lung disease
topics.summary: Insidious exertional dyspnea with a persistent dry cough with fine bibasilar inspiratory crackles likened to opening hook-and-loop fastener is the presentation that defines interstitial lung disease. High-resolution CT of the chest confirms it, and multidisciplinary evaluation before any disease-specific therapy is the initial management.

topics.title: Tuberculosis
topics.summary: Three weeks of cough, night sweats, and unintentional weight loss with a thin, chronically ill appearance with apical crackles is the presentation that defines tuberculosis. Sputum for acid-fast smear and nucleic acid amplification testing confirms it, and combination antimycobacterial therapy with public health notification is the initial management.

topics.title: Lung cancer
topics.summary: Six weeks of cough with one episode of blood-streaked sputum with clubbing of the fingers with a fixed localized wheeze is the presentation that defines lung cancer. CT of the chest with tissue sampling of the dominant lesion confirms it, and staging evaluation before treatment selection is the initial management.

topics.title: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
topics.summary: Rapidly worsening breathlessness twelve hours after a severe systemic insult with diffuse bilateral crackles with refractory hypoxemia is the presentation that defines acute respiratory distress syndrome. Chest imaging with assessment of oxygenation ratio confirms it, and lung-protective ventilation with low tidal volumes is the initial management.

topics.title: Pulmonary hypertension
topics.summary: Progressive exertional dyspnea with exertional presyncope with a loud pulmonic component of the second heart sound with a parasternal heave is the presentation that defines pulmonary hypertension. Transthoracic echocardiography followed by right heart catheterization confirms it, and referral to a specialized center for hemodynamic confirmation is the initial management.

chapters.name: Gastroenterology
chapters.blurb: Luminal disease, pancreaticobiliary disorders, and liver medicine.

topics.title: Gastroesophageal reflux disease
topics.summary: Retrosternal burning after meals that worsens when lying flat with an unremarkable abdominal examination with a normal weight trend is the presentation that defines gastroesophageal reflux disease. An empiric trial of acid suppression without initial testing confirms it, and once-daily proton pump inhibitor therapy with lifestyle modification is the initial management.

topics.title: Peptic ulcer disease
topics.summary: Gnawing epigastric pain that improves with meals then recurs with mild epigastric tenderness without peritoneal signs is the presentation that defines peptic ulcer disease. Testing for Helicobacter pylori infection confirms it, and acid suppression with eradication therapy when infection is confirmed is the initial management.

topics.title: Crohn disease
topics.summary: Three months of crampy abdominal pain, non-bloody diarrhea, and weight loss with a tender right lower quadrant fullness with perianal skin tags is the presentation that defines crohn disease. Ileocolonoscopy with biopsies confirms it, and induction therapy selected by disease severity and location is the initial management.

topics.title: Ulcerative colitis
topics.summary: Six weeks of bloody diarrhea with urgency and tenesmus with left lower quadrant tenderness with visible blood on rectal examination is the presentation that defines ulcerative colitis. Colonoscopy with biopsies after infection is excluded confirms it, and induction therapy scaled to endoscopic severity is the initial management.

topics.title: Celiac disease
topics.summary: Chronic bloating, loose stools, and fatigue with iron deficiency with a thin habitus with pallor and an itchy vesicular rash on the elbows is the presentation that defines celiac disease. Tissue transglutaminase serology while on a gluten-containing diet confirms it, and a strict gluten-free diet with dietitian support is the initial management.

topics.title: Cirrhosis with portal hypertension
topics.summary: Increasing abdominal girth with ankle swelling with shifting dullness, spider angiomata, and palmar erythema is the presentation that defines cirrhosis with portal hypertension. Abdominal ultrasonography with diagnostic paracentesis confirms it, and sodium restriction and diuretic therapy with variceal screening is the initial management.

topics.title: Acute pancreatitis
topics.summary: Sudden severe epigastric pain boring through to the back with vomiting with epigastric guarding with hypoactive bowel sounds is the presentation that defines acute pancreatitis. Serum lipase measurement confirms it, and early goal-directed intravenous fluids with analgesia is the initial management.

topics.title: Choledocholithiasis
topics.summary: Right upper quadrant pain with dark urine and pale stools with scleral icterus with right upper quadrant tenderness is the presentation that defines choledocholithiasis. Right upper quadrant ultrasonography with liver chemistries confirms it, and endoscopic clearance of the duct followed by cholecystectomy is the initial management.

topics.title: Clostridioides difficile colitis
topics.summary: Profuse watery diarrhea beginning days after a course of antibiotics with lower abdominal tenderness with low-grade fever is the presentation that defines clostridioides difficile colitis. Stool testing for the organism and its toxin confirms it, and oral standard-of-care antibiotic therapy with cessation of the inciting agent is the initial management.

topics.title: Irritable bowel syndrome
topics.summary: Six months of crampy abdominal pain relieved by defecation, with variable stool form with a soft abdomen with mild diffuse tenderness and no alarm features is the presentation that defines irritable bowel syndrome. A positive symptom-based diagnosis with limited targeted testing confirms it, and dietary modification with symptom-directed therapy and reassurance is the initial management.

topics.title: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding
topics.summary: Two episodes of coffee-ground emesis with black tarry stools with resting tachycardia with melena on rectal examination is the presentation that defines upper gastrointestinal bleeding. Hemodynamic assessment with early risk stratification confirms it, and volume resuscitation, acid suppression, and endoscopy after stabilization is the initial management.

topics.title: Chronic hepatitis
topics.summary: An incidental finding of elevated aminotransferases on routine testing with a soft, nontender abdomen with no stigmata of chronic disease is the presentation that defines chronic hepatitis. Viral serologies with metabolic and autoimmune screening confirms it, and therapy directed at the specific underlying cause is the initial management.

chapters.name: Nephrology
chapters.blurb: Acute and chronic kidney disease, electrolytes, and acid–base.

topics.title: Prerenal acute kidney injury
topics.summary: Two days of vomiting and poor intake with reduced urine output with dry mucous membranes with a 12-point orthostatic pulse increment is the presentation that defines prerenal acute kidney injury. Urine studies with a fractional excretion of sodium confirms it, and isotonic intravenous volume repletion is the initial management.

topics.title: Acute tubular necrosis
topics.summary: Oliguria following prolonged intraoperative hypotension with muddy brown granular casts on urine microscopy is the presentation that defines acute tubular necrosis. Urine microscopy with serial chemistries confirms it, and supportive care with careful fluid and electrolyte management is the initial management.

topics.title: Nephrotic syndrome
topics.summary: Progressive leg swelling with frothy urine with periorbital edema with 3+ proteinuria on dipstick is the presentation that defines nephrotic syndrome. Quantification of proteinuria with serologic evaluation confirms it, and renin-angiotensin blockade with edema management and biopsy consideration is the initial management.

topics.title: IgA nephropathy
topics.summary: Cola-colored urine two days after an upper respiratory infection with mild hypertension with red cell casts on microscopy is the presentation that defines igA nephropathy. Urinalysis with quantified proteinuria and kidney function confirms it, and blood pressure control with renin-angiotensin blockade is the initial management.

topics.title: Nephrolithiasis
topics.summary: Sudden colicky flank pain radiating to the groin with nausea with a patient writhing, unable to find a comfortable position, with hematuria is the presentation that defines nephrolithiasis. Noncontrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis confirms it, and analgesia, hydration, and medical expulsive therapy for suitable stones is the initial management.

topics.title: Hyperkalemia
topics.summary: Palpitations and generalized weakness in a patient on renin-angiotensin blockade with peaked symmetric T waves on the electrocardiogram is the presentation that defines hyperkalemia. Immediate electrocardiography with repeat chemistries confirms it, and intravenous calcium followed by potassium-shifting and removal therapy is the initial management.

topics.title: Hyponatremia from inappropriate antidiuresis
topics.summary: Gradual confusion and unsteadiness without volume loss with euvolemia on examination with concentrated urine despite low serum sodium is the presentation that defines hyponatremia from inappropriate antidiuresis. Paired serum and urine osmolality with urine sodium confirms it, and fluid restriction with treatment of the underlying trigger is the initial management.

topics.title: Chronic kidney disease
topics.summary: An elevated creatinine found on two tests three months apart with well-controlled blood pressure with trace edema is the presentation that defines chronic kidney disease. Urine albumin quantification with kidney ultrasonography confirms it, and risk-factor control with renin-angiotensin blockade and staged monitoring is the initial management.

topics.title: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
topics.summary: Chronic dull flank fullness with episodic hematuria and a strong family history with bilateral palpable flank masses with elevated blood pressure is the presentation that defines autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. Abdominal ultrasonography with family-based counseling confirms it, and aggressive blood pressure control with disease-specific referral is the initial management.

topics.title: Renal artery stenosis
topics.summary: Resistant hypertension despite three antihypertensive agents with an abdominal bruit with a rise in creatinine after starting renin-angiotensin blockade is the presentation that defines renal artery stenosis. Duplex ultrasonography or CT angiography of the renal arteries confirms it, and optimized medical antihypertensive therapy is the initial management.

topics.title: Anion gap metabolic acidosis
topics.summary: Deep sighing respirations with malaise in an unwell patient with tachypnea with fruity breath odor and dry mucous membranes is the presentation that defines anion gap metabolic acidosis. Blood gas analysis with chemistry panel and gap calculation confirms it, and treatment of the underlying driver with monitored correction is the initial management.

topics.title: Pyelonephritis
topics.summary: Two days of fever, flank pain, and burning urination with costovertebral angle tenderness with a temperature of 38.6°C is the presentation that defines pyelonephritis. Urinalysis with urine culture before antibiotics confirms it, and empiric antibiotic therapy adjusted to culture results is the initial management.

chapters.name: Endocrinology
chapters.blurb: Glycemic disorders, thyroid and adrenal disease, and bone metabolism.

topics.title: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
topics.summary: Fatigue, thirst, and nocturia over several months with an elevated body mass index with velvety darkening of the neck creases is the presentation that defines type 2 diabetes mellitus. Hemoglobin A1c or fasting glucose confirmation confirms it, and metformin with structured lifestyle modification is the initial management.

topics.title: Diabetic ketoacidosis
topics.summary: A day of vomiting, abdominal pain, and rapid breathing in an insulin-dependent patient with deep regular respirations with a fruity breath odor is the presentation that defines diabetic ketoacidosis. Glucose, ketones, and blood gas measurement confirms it, and intravenous fluids, insulin infusion, and potassium replacement by protocol is the initial management.

topics.title: Primary hypothyroidism
topics.summary: Fatigue, weight gain, constipation, and cold intolerance with dry skin, bradycardia, and delayed relaxation of the ankle reflexes is the presentation that defines primary hypothyroidism. Serum thyroid-stimulating hormone measurement confirms it, and weight-based levothyroxine replacement is the initial management.

topics.title: Graves disease
topics.summary: Palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor, and unintentional weight loss with a diffusely enlarged thyroid with lid lag and a fine tremor is the presentation that defines graves disease. Thyroid-stimulating hormone with receptor antibody testing confirms it, and a beta blocker for symptoms with definitive antithyroid therapy is the initial management.

topics.title: Thyroid nodule
topics.summary: A painless anterior neck lump noticed while shaving with a firm 1.8 cm nodule that moves with swallowing, without adenopathy is the presentation that defines thyroid nodule. Thyroid-stimulating hormone measurement with neck ultrasonography confirms it, and risk-stratified follow-up or biopsy by sonographic criteria is the initial management.

topics.title: Cushing syndrome
topics.summary: Weight gain, easy bruising, and proximal muscle weakness with central adiposity with wide violaceous striae and facial plethora is the presentation that defines cushing syndrome. An overnight dexamethasone suppression or late-night salivary cortisol test confirms it, and confirmation of excess before any localizing imaging is the initial management.

topics.title: Adrenal insufficiency
topics.summary: Progressive fatigue, salt craving, and dizziness on standing with hyperpigmented palmar creases with low blood pressure is the presentation that defines adrenal insufficiency. Early-morning cortisol with corticotropin stimulation testing confirms it, and glucocorticoid replacement with stress-dose education is the initial management.

topics.title: Primary hyperparathyroidism
topics.summary: Kidney stones with vague bone aches and low mood with an unremarkable examination with incidental hypercalcemia on labs is the presentation that defines primary hyperparathyroidism. Paired serum calcium and parathyroid hormone measurement confirms it, and surgical evaluation when operative criteria are met is the initial management.

topics.title: Osteoporosis
topics.summary: A wrist fracture after a fall from standing height with thoracic kyphosis with 3 cm of measured height loss is the presentation that defines osteoporosis. Dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry confirms it, and antiresorptive therapy with calcium, vitamin D, and fall-risk reduction is the initial management.

topics.title: Prolactinoma
topics.summary: A year of absent menses with milky nipple discharge with expressible galactorrhea with bitemporal visual field constriction is the presentation that defines prolactinoma. Serum prolactin followed by pituitary magnetic resonance imaging confirms it, and dopamine agonist therapy is the initial management.

topics.title: Pheochromocytoma
topics.summary: Episodic pounding headaches, sweating, and palpitations with a blood pressure of 196/108 mm Hg during a witnessed episode is the presentation that defines pheochromocytoma. Plasma or urinary metanephrine measurement confirms it, and alpha blockade before beta blockade and definitive surgery is the initial management.

topics.title: Polycystic ovary syndrome
topics.summary: Irregular infrequent menses with worsening facial hair growth with hirsutism and acne with an elevated body mass index is the presentation that defines polycystic ovary syndrome. Targeted hormonal testing to exclude mimics confirms it, and lifestyle modification with combined hormonal therapy when contraception is desired is the initial management.

chapters.name: Infectious Disease
chapters.blurb: Community and healthcare-associated infection, and the febrile patient.

topics.title: Cellulitis
topics.summary: Two days of spreading warmth and redness over the lower leg with a poorly demarcated, warm, tender erythematous plaque with linear streaking is the presentation that defines cellulitis. Clinical diagnosis with marking of the advancing border confirms it, and empiric antibiotic therapy covering streptococci is the initial management.

topics.title: Bacterial meningitis
topics.summary: Twelve hours of fever, severe headache, and confusion with nuchal rigidity with photophobia and a temperature of 39.1°C is the presentation that defines bacterial meningitis. Blood cultures with lumbar puncture confirms it, and immediate empiric antibiotics with adjunctive glucocorticoids is the initial management.

topics.title: Infectious mononucleosis
topics.summary: A week of sore throat, fatigue, and fever in a college student with symmetric posterior cervical adenopathy with splenomegaly and exudative tonsils is the presentation that defines infectious mononucleosis. Heterophile antibody testing with a peripheral smear confirms it, and supportive care with activity restriction to protect the spleen is the initial management.

topics.title: Influenza
topics.summary: Abrupt fever, myalgias, dry cough, and headache in winter with an ill-appearing patient with a temperature of 38.9°C and clear lung fields is the presentation that defines influenza. Rapid molecular testing during circulating season confirms it, and early antiviral therapy for those at elevated risk is the initial management.

topics.title: Human immunodeficiency virus infection
topics.summary: Two weeks of fever, sore throat, and a faint truncal rash after a new exposure with diffuse lymphadenopathy with mucosal ulcerations is the presentation that defines human immunodeficiency virus infection. Combined antigen-antibody testing with confirmatory viral load confirms it, and prompt initiation of antiretroviral therapy with linkage to care is the initial management.

topics.title: Lyme disease
topics.summary: An expanding annular rash with fatigue after hiking in an endemic area with a 9 cm erythematous patch with central clearing on the thigh is the presentation that defines lyme disease. Clinical diagnosis when the classic rash is present confirms it, and a course of oral doxycycline is the initial management.

topics.title: Osteomyelitis
topics.summary: Three weeks of worsening focal bone pain with low-grade fever with point tenderness over the tibia with overlying warmth is the presentation that defines osteomyelitis. Magnetic resonance imaging with cultures before antibiotics confirms it, and prolonged targeted antibiotic therapy with surgical consultation is the initial management.

topics.title: Urinary tract infection
topics.summary: Two days of burning urination with frequency and urgency with suprapubic tenderness without flank pain or fever is the presentation that defines urinary tract infection. Urinalysis; culture reserved for complicated presentations confirms it, and a short course of first-line oral antibiotics is the initial management.

topics.title: Herpes zoster
topics.summary: Three days of burning pain followed by a blistering rash on one side of the trunk with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base in a single dermatome, sparing the midline is the presentation that defines herpes zoster. Clinical diagnosis by the dermatomal pattern confirms it, and oral antiviral therapy started within 72 hours of rash onset is the initial management.

topics.title: Sepsis
topics.summary: Fever, rigors, and confusion progressing over hours with hypotension with mottled extremities and delayed capillary refill is the presentation that defines sepsis. Blood cultures with serum lactate before antibiotics confirms it, and broad-spectrum antibiotics within the first hour and measured fluid resuscitation is the initial management.

topics.title: Infective diarrhea
topics.summary: Three days of watery diarrhea and cramping after a restaurant meal with diffuse abdominal tenderness with hyperactive bowel sounds and dry mucosa is the presentation that defines infective diarrhea. Supportive diagnosis; stool studies for severe or prolonged cases confirms it, and oral rehydration with symptom-guided supportive care is the initial management.

topics.title: Latent tuberculosis infection
topics.summary: A positive tuberculosis screening test found before starting immunosuppression with a completely normal examination with a normal chest radiograph is the presentation that defines latent tuberculosis infection. Interferon-gamma release assay with chest radiography confirms it, and preventive single-drug therapy after active disease is excluded is the initial management.

chapters.name: Neurology
chapters.blurb: Cerebrovascular disease, headache, movement disorders, and neuromuscular illness.

topics.title: Acute ischemic stroke
topics.summary: Abrupt right-sided weakness and slurred speech beginning 70 minutes ago with right facial droop, dysarthria, and 3/5 strength in the right arm is the presentation that defines acute ischemic stroke. Immediate noncontrast CT of the head confirms it, and thrombolytic evaluation against the treatment window is the initial management.

topics.title: Transient ischemic attack
topics.summary: Fifteen minutes of left arm weakness and garbled speech, now fully resolved with a normal neurologic examination with an irregular pulse is the presentation that defines transient ischemic attack. Urgent vascular and cardiac source evaluation confirms it, and antiplatelet therapy with aggressive risk factor control is the initial management.

topics.title: Migraine
topics.summary: Recurrent unilateral throbbing headaches with nausea and light sensitivity with a normal neurologic examination between and during episodes is the presentation that defines migraine. Clinical diagnosis by established criteria confirms it, and abortive therapy at onset with trigger management is the initial management.

topics.title: Tension-type headache
topics.summary: Band-like bilateral head pressure on stressful workdays with pericranial muscle tenderness with an otherwise normal examination is the presentation that defines tension-type headache. Clinical diagnosis with screening for red flags confirms it, and simple analgesia with attention to sleep, posture, and stress is the initial management.

topics.title: Parkinson disease
topics.summary: Two years of progressive slowness, small handwriting, and a resting hand tremor with cogwheel rigidity, hypomimia, and a 4-Hz pill-rolling tremor is the presentation that defines parkinson disease. Clinical diagnosis by cardinal motor features confirms it, and dopaminergic therapy timed to functional impact is the initial management.

topics.title: Multiple sclerosis
topics.summary: Painful vision loss in one eye a year after an episode of leg numbness with an afferent pupillary defect with hyperreflexia in the legs is the presentation that defines multiple sclerosis. Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain and spinal cord confirms it, and high-dose glucocorticoids for the acute relapse with disease-modifying therapy is the initial management.

topics.title: Guillain-Barré syndrome
topics.summary: Ascending leg weakness and tingling ten days after a diarrheal illness with symmetric proximal and distal weakness with absent ankle reflexes is the presentation that defines guillain-Barré syndrome. Lumbar puncture with serial bedside spirometry confirms it, and immunomodulatory therapy with close respiratory monitoring is the initial management.

topics.title: Myasthenia gravis
topics.summary: Evening drooping of the eyelids and double vision that worsens through the day with fatigable ptosis on sustained upgaze with normal pupils is the presentation that defines myasthenia gravis. Acetylcholine receptor antibody testing confirms it, and an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor with immunotherapy planning is the initial management.

topics.title: Focal epilepsy
topics.summary: Three stereotyped episodes of arm jerking with impaired awareness with a normal interictal examination with tongue-bite healing is the presentation that defines focal epilepsy. Electroencephalography with magnetic resonance imaging confirms it, and a single antiseizure medication titrated to control is the initial management.

topics.title: Essential tremor
topics.summary: Ten years of slowly progressive hand shaking, worse when pouring coffee with a symmetric 8-Hz action tremor with none at rest, improved after wine is the presentation that defines essential tremor. Clinical diagnosis with medication review confirms it, and propranolol or primidone when function is impaired is the initial management.

topics.title: Carpal tunnel syndrome
topics.summary: Nighttime numb awakening of the thumb and first two fingers with thenar sensory loss with a positive wrist-flexion provocation and thenar wasting is the presentation that defines carpal tunnel syndrome. Clinical diagnosis; nerve conduction studies when surgery is considered confirms it, and nocturnal wrist splinting with activity modification is the initial management.

topics.title: Delirium
topics.summary: One day of fluctuating confusion and agitation in a hospitalized older adult with waxing and waning attention with disorientation and daytime somnolence is the presentation that defines delirium. Structured bedside assessment with a targeted precipitant search confirms it, and treatment of precipitants with nonpharmacologic reorientation is the initial management.

chapters.name: Hematology & Oncology
chapters.blurb: Anemias, cytopenias, hematologic malignancy, and oncologic emergencies.

topics.title: Iron deficiency anemia
topics.summary: Three months of fatigue and exertional breathlessness with conjunctival pallor with spoon-shaped nails and a craving for ice is the presentation that defines iron deficiency anemia. Iron studies with ferritin measurement confirms it, and oral iron replacement with a search for the source of loss is the initial management.

topics.title: Vitamin B12 deficiency
topics.summary: Gradual fatigue with numb, tingling feet and unsteady gait with pallor, reduced vibratory sense, and impaired position sense at the toes is the presentation that defines vitamin B12 deficiency. Serum B12 with methylmalonic acid confirmation confirms it, and parenteral B12 repletion is the initial management.

topics.title: Immune thrombocytopenia
topics.summary: A week of easy bruising and gum bleeding in an otherwise well person with scattered petechiae over the shins with an otherwise normal examination is the presentation that defines immune thrombocytopenia. Complete blood count with peripheral smear review confirms it, and glucocorticoids when counts are dangerously low; observation otherwise is the initial management.

topics.title: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
topics.summary: Two days of confusion and dark urine in a previously healthy adult with pallor, scattered petechiae, and waxing-waning neurologic signs is the presentation that defines thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura. Peripheral smear with hemolysis labs and enzyme activity testing confirms it, and urgent plasma exchange is the initial management.

topics.title: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia
topics.summary: An abnormal white cell count found on a routine blood count with small rubbery cervical nodes with mild splenomegaly is the presentation that defines chronic lymphocytic leukemia. Flow cytometry of peripheral blood confirms it, and observation for early asymptomatic disease is the initial management.

topics.title: Chronic myeloid leukemia
topics.summary: Early satiety and drenching night sweats over two months with a spleen palpable 8 cm below the costal margin is the presentation that defines chronic myeloid leukemia. Molecular testing for the fusion transcript confirms it, and tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy is the initial management.

topics.title: Multiple myeloma
topics.summary: Three months of low back pain, fatigue, and recurrent infections with vertebral point tenderness with pallor is the presentation that defines multiple myeloma. Serum protein electrophoresis with free light chains and marrow biopsy confirms it, and combination therapy with skeletal protection is the initial management.

topics.title: Hodgkin lymphoma
topics.summary: A painless enlarging neck mass with drenching night sweats with a firm rubbery 3 cm supraclavicular node with intermittent fever is the presentation that defines hodgkin lymphoma. Excisional lymph node biopsy confirms it, and staging followed by combination chemotherapy is the initial management.

topics.title: Sickle cell disease with vaso-occlusive crisis
topics.topic: Sickle cell disease with vaso-occlusive crisis
topics.summary: Eight hours of severe diffuse bone pain in a patient with known disease with tachycardia and distress without focal findings; oxygen saturation 97% is the presentation that defines sickle cell disease with vaso-occlusive crisis. Clinical diagnosis with labs to exclude complications confirms it, and prompt analgesia with hydration and incentive spirometry is the initial management.

topics.title: Polycythemia vera
topics.summary: Generalized itching after hot showers with persistent facial redness with facial plethora with splenomegaly and an elevated hematocrit is the presentation that defines polycythemia vera. Erythropoietin level with driver mutation testing confirms it, and serial phlebotomy with low-dose aspirin is the initial management.

topics.title: Tumor lysis syndrome
topics.summary: Weakness and reduced urine output two days after starting chemotherapy with tetanic muscle cramps with an irregular pulse is the presentation that defines tumor lysis syndrome. Serial chemistries including urate, potassium, phosphorus, and calcium confirms it, and aggressive hydration with urate-lowering therapy is the initial management.

topics.title: Cancer screening decision
topics.summary: A scheduled preventive care review with no current complaints with an entirely normal age-appropriate examination is the presentation that defines cancer screening decision. Guideline-based, age- and risk-stratified screening selection confirms it, and shared decision-making documented with intervals set is the initial management.

chapters.name: Rheumatology
chapters.blurb: Inflammatory arthritis, connective tissue disease, and the vasculitides.

topics.title: Rheumatoid arthritis
topics.summary: Three months of symmetric hand pain and swelling with an hour of morning stiffness with boggy synovitis of the metacarpophalangeal and wrist joints bilaterally is the presentation that defines rheumatoid arthritis. Inflammatory markers with autoantibody testing confirms it, and early disease-modifying therapy with methotrexate is the initial management.

topics.title: Osteoarthritis
topics.summary: Two years of knee pain that worsens with use and eases with rest with bony enlargement with crepitus and brief stiffness after sitting is the presentation that defines osteoarthritis. Weight-bearing radiography when the diagnosis is unclear confirms it, and exercise therapy, weight management, and topical anti-inflammatory agents is the initial management.

topics.title: Gout
topics.summary: A great-toe joint that became exquisitely painful overnight with a red, swollen, shiny first metatarsophalangeal joint too tender for a bedsheet is the presentation that defines gout. Arthrocentesis with polarized light microscopy confirms it, and an anti-inflammatory agent chosen by comorbidity profile is the initial management.

topics.title: Calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease
topics.summary: An acutely swollen knee in an older adult without trauma with a warm knee effusion with chondrocalcinosis on radiography is the presentation that defines calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease. Arthrocentesis with crystal analysis and infection exclusion confirms it, and joint aspiration with an intra-articular or systemic anti-inflammatory is the initial management.

topics.title: Systemic lupus erythematosus
topics.summary: Three months of fatigue, joint pain, and a facial rash worse after sun with a malar rash sparing the nasolabial folds with small-joint synovitis is the presentation that defines systemic lupus erythematosus. Antinuclear antibody testing followed by specific serologies confirms it, and hydroxychloroquine as foundation therapy is the initial management.

topics.title: Polymyalgia rheumatica
topics.summary: Three weeks of severe shoulder and hip girdle stiffness, worst on waking with painful restriction of shoulder elevation without true weakness is the presentation that defines polymyalgia rheumatica. Inflammatory marker measurement confirms it, and low-dose glucocorticoids with a planned taper is the initial management.

topics.title: Giant cell arteritis
topics.summary: A new temporal headache with jaw fatigue while chewing with a tender, thickened temporal artery with scalp sensitivity is the presentation that defines giant cell arteritis. Inflammatory markers with prompt temporal artery biopsy confirms it, and immediate high-dose glucocorticoids before biopsy confirmation is the initial management.

topics.title: Ankylosing spondylitis
topics.summary: Two years of low back stiffness that improves with exercise and wakes him at night with reduced lumbar flexion with sacroiliac joint tenderness is the presentation that defines ankylosing spondylitis. Sacroiliac imaging with inflammatory back pain criteria confirms it, and a structured exercise program with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory therapy is the initial management.

topics.title: Fibromyalgia
topics.summary: A year of widespread pain, unrefreshing sleep, and mental fog with diffuse soft-tissue tenderness with a normal joint examination is the presentation that defines fibromyalgia. Clinical diagnosis with limited testing to exclude mimics confirms it, and graded aerobic exercise, sleep care, and centrally acting therapy is the initial management.

topics.title: Septic arthritis
topics.summary: A hot swollen knee with fever and refusal to bear weight with a tense effusion held in slight flexion, exquisitely painful with any motion is the presentation that defines septic arthritis. Immediate arthrocentesis with synovial fluid analysis and cultures confirms it, and empiric intravenous antibiotics with drainage of the joint is the initial management.

topics.title: Sjögren syndrome
topics.summary: A year of gritty dry eyes and a mouth too dry to swallow crackers with reduced salivary pooling with dental caries along the gumline is the presentation that defines sjögren syndrome. Autoantibody testing with objective dryness measures confirms it, and symptomatic moisture replacement with regular dental care is the initial management.

topics.title: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
topics.summary: Six weeks of sinus crusting, nosebleeds, and new blood in the urine with nasal crusting with a saddle-nose contour and dysmorphic red cells in urine is the presentation that defines granulomatosis with polyangiitis. Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody testing with tissue biopsy confirms it, and induction immunosuppression is the initial management.

chapters.name: Psychiatry
chapters.blurb: Mood, anxiety, psychotic, and substance use disorders in the medical setting.

topics.title: Major depressive disorder
topics.summary: Six weeks of low mood, poor sleep, and loss of interest in hobbies with flat affect with psychomotor slowing and passive death wish, without plan is the presentation that defines major depressive disorder. Structured screening with direct safety assessment confirms it, and an antidepressant with psychotherapy and scheduled follow-up is the initial management.

topics.title: Generalized anxiety disorder
topics.summary: Eight months of uncontrollable worry about work, health, and family with restlessness with muscle tension and impaired concentration is the presentation that defines generalized anxiety disorder. Clinical diagnosis with screening scales confirms it, and cognitive behavioral therapy with a serotonergic agent is the initial management.

topics.title: Panic disorder
topics.summary: Recurrent abrupt episodes of pounding heart, breathlessness, and fear of dying with a normal cardiac examination after a witnessed spell resolves within minutes is the presentation that defines panic disorder. Clinical diagnosis after targeted medical exclusion confirms it, and cognitive behavioral therapy with a serotonergic agent is the initial management.

topics.title: Bipolar I disorder
topics.summary: Five days of decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, and spending sprees with expansive mood with flight of ideas and distractibility is the presentation that defines bipolar I disorder. Clinical diagnosis with substance and medical exclusion confirms it, and a mood stabilizer with monitored safety planning is the initial management.

topics.title: Schizophrenia
topics.summary: Eight months of social withdrawal, muttering to himself, and fixed persecutory beliefs with auditory hallucinations with disorganized speech and blunted affect is the presentation that defines schizophrenia. Clinical diagnosis with first-episode medical workup confirms it, and an antipsychotic with coordinated specialty care is the initial management.

topics.title: Post-traumatic stress disorder
topics.summary: Four months of nightmares and hypervigilance after a serious vehicle collision with an exaggerated startle response with avoidance of driving is the presentation that defines post-traumatic stress disorder. Structured trauma-focused assessment confirms it, and trauma-focused psychotherapy with adjunctive medication is the initial management.

topics.title: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
topics.summary: Two hours daily of intrusive contamination thoughts and ritualized washing with chapped, cracked hands with insight that the fears are excessive is the presentation that defines obsessive-compulsive disorder. Clinical diagnosis with severity scaling confirms it, and exposure and response prevention with a serotonergic agent is the initial management.

topics.title: Adjustment disorder
topics.summary: Three weeks of tearfulness and poor focus after a job loss with a congruent, reactive affect without vegetative signs is the presentation that defines adjustment disorder. Clinical diagnosis anchored to the stressor timeline confirms it, and brief supportive psychotherapy is the initial management.

topics.title: Alcohol use disorder
topics.summary: Escalating evening drinking with morning shakiness and two failed cuts with a fine tremor with hepatomegaly and mildly elevated pulse is the presentation that defines alcohol use disorder. Structured screening with severity staging confirms it, and motivational interviewing with pharmacotherapy and withdrawal risk planning is the initial management.

topics.title: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
topics.summary: Lifelong distractibility and disorganization now impairing a first job with fidgetiness with a history reaching back to primary school is the presentation that defines attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. Structured diagnostic interview with collateral history confirms it, and stimulant therapy with organizational skills coaching is the initial management.

topics.title: Insomnia disorder
topics.summary: Four months of 90-minute sleep onset with daytime exhaustion with a tired but alert adult with an unremarkable examination is the presentation that defines insomnia disorder. Sleep history with diary or actigraphy confirms it, and cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia as first-line treatment is the initial management.

topics.title: Somatic symptom disorder
topics.summary: A year of disabling concern over fluctuating pains despite reassuring evaluations with a thick folder of normal results with high health anxiety is the presentation that defines somatic symptom disorder. Review of records with a single-clinician care plan confirms it, and regularly scheduled visits with one clinician and graded activity is the initial management.
